executive_delta.template: Factory-gate inflation broadened upstream: PPI YoY rose from {obs:cn_ppi_yoy@2026-09} to {obs:cn_ppi_yoy@2026-10}, led by producer goods at {obs:cn_ppi_producer_yoy@2026-10}, as the NBS release {src:event_7c0e35a3eee519ffe8ae} reports.
Monthly momentum cooled: PPI MoM eased from {obs:cn_ppi_mom@2026-09} to {obs:cn_ppi_mom@2026-10}, although its three-month average is still {drv:ma(cn_ppi_mom,3)@2026-10}.

The rise has not reached consumers: consumer-goods PPI is still {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-10} and core CPI slipped to {obs:cn_core_cpi_yoy@2026-10}, a change of {drv:diff(cn_core_cpi_yoy,1)@2026-10} on the month.

hypothesis_impact.rationale_template: Upstream prices keep the price-turn case alive, but no test flipped and the gain is concentrated in producer goods.
Weaker core CPI at {obs:cn_core_cpi_yoy@2026-10} gives no sign that private demand is pulling prices up.
This release carries no new fiscal or credit data; the PBOC relending notice is a market-support tool, not a broad demand impulse.
Price data say nothing new about external demand.

hypothesis_impact.divergence_reason: No test flipped, but the gap between producer goods at {obs:cn_ppi_producer_yoy@2026-10} and consumer goods at {obs:cn_ppi_consumer_yoy@2026-10} widened: the rule only checks the sign of consumer-goods prices, not how far upstream prices run ahead of them.
hypothesis_impact.rationale_template: An upstream-led rise with flat consumer goods prices is what a cost-push bounce looks like.

preliminary_implications.template: Whether margins absorb the upstream rise is the next test of the price turn.
